newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-HILL RESPONDS TO HIS CRITICS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL RESPONDS TO HIS CRITICS.

text.p: Under-fire world champion Damon Hill responded to his critics on Friday after trailing in a dismal 20th in free practice for Sunday's British Grand Prix.
He said he was trying his hardest for the Arrows team despite being criticsed by his Arrows team boss Tom Walkinshaw for not driving like a champion.
He also said he understood how Walkinshaw felt and sympathised with him.
"It is a very difficult year for Tom as well as for me. It simply has not gone as well as we had hoped," said Hill.
"Sometimes frustration is evident not only in drivers, but also in team managers. Now, we have to work very hard, as hard as we can, to rectify the situation."
Hill spoke in a calm and dignified way as a mass of reporters squeezed up to the entrance to the Arrows motor home in the paddock.
"We always get on well and we are concentrating together on how to make the whole thing work better. I talk to him about how to make the situation at Arrows better for everyone.

"One could say that the fact that one of the better engine deals in the paddock went to another team did not help the situation for Tom....But he is looking hard at finding a decent horsepower package for next year.

"My goal is to see what the future holds and to get back in the hunt for a world championship as soon as possible. I would like it to be with the Arrows' team if they are able to offer me that package."

Hill said that any team boss was entitled to "put a rocket up the bum of his drivers whenever he wants to -- every team manager does that. I've had much worse criticism from other team managers in the past...."

Asked about his effort, he said: "I've given it everything I can. I am a professional. When I get in the car I always want to give it my best performance and I don't want to let anyone down, least of all myself.

"But these things happen -- like me being outqualified by Pedro from time to time. Pedro (Diniz, his Brazilian team-mate) is there to show what he can do and I am out here trying to get from the car whatever I can.
"Last year, I managed to get the car on the front row of the grid at every single race (albeit in a Williams not an Arrows) and that is something that no-one has ever done before."
Earlier Walkinshaw had denied widespread reported claims that he had said he would dismiss Hill later this year if he failed to improve his performances.

But Hill receivecd support from an unexpected source when Renault's top engineer Bernard Dudot, who worked with him at Williams for five years, said the team was badly missing him and would be leading the world championship if he had stayed.
